Sarah / Ava — quick legal note on the erasure language and SCCs:

1) Erasure/Backups: We can accept the 30-day operational erasure commitment for active systems. For immutable backups, we propose the following compromise (included in Redlines-accepted-alternatives_20260531.pdf): Redwood will mark the account data for deletion and permanently remove it from active storage within 30 days, and remove it from backups by the next scheduled backup cycle (not to exceed 45 days). That gives Northbridge the operational guarantee you need while preserving established backup retention.

2) SCCs / International transfers: Northbridge requested a clause that would require prior notice and consent for any new subprocessor outside the EEA. While we typically operate with a global subprocessor model and rely on SCCs where needed, we can add a 30-day notice requirement for new subprocessors that will process regulated EU personal data. That is reflected in the attached markup.

3) DPIA: If Northbridge believes a DPIA is required, our privacy team will provide a DPIA input pack and local data flow diagrams — Neha, please prepare the pack once Sarah confirms.

If those alternatives are acceptable I recommend we proceed to signature.

Rishi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
